title: Quantized projection: grouped W8/W4 integers with FP32 group scales, or NVFP4
description: quantized-projections' formats, chosen by `format`. int8 and int4, its G32 representation: each group of `group` weights shares one represented FP32 scale, codes are signed 8 or 4 bits, and the projection multiplies the decoded values. nvfp4, its NVFP4 codec and scalar FP64 projection: E2M1 codes in adjacent nibbles, E4M3 block scales per 16 and one global scale, each block decoded once and reused for every token row (four_over_six scales a block to 4 instead of 6 where that lowers the error). An optimized kernel consumes the same codes, scales and accumulation contract. Its device form loads a checkpoint's stored BF16, FP8 (per channel or per tensor), MXFP8 and NVFP4 matrices on the engine's device and multiplies them through cuBLASLt with torch's scaled matmul (code/device_matrices.py): FP8 activations per row, NVFP4 activations per 16-value block (W4A4), FP32 accumulation; with activations bf16 an NVFP4 matrix keeps 16-bit activations (W4A16), and with fp8_activations bf16 an FP8 one (W8A16), the matrix decoded a chunk of rows at a time for the prompt GEMMs; NVFP4 matrices stacked by rows keep one global scale per row. Decode rows (calls of up to decode_rows, 16) run on crit's kernels, built for the engine's device with the engine's tuning or their default knobs: mma-rows' tensor-core tile (gemv mma; short prompts too, tile_rows) or decode-gemv's GEMVs (code/device_nvfp4.py); prompt GEMMs on cuBLASLt, or with prompt_gemm pinned on crit's kernel pinned-gemm (one split-K-free algorithm per shape and format, a prompt row's bits the same at every length), with fixed_tiles on crit's kernel fixed-tile-gemm, and with tile on mma-rows' prompt tile (every prompt row with the bits it has as a decode row: the facts' prompt_exact, for preserve mode's honesty); each with a torch fallback of the same row invariance. A draft-only matrix (an MTP layer, a draft head) may be re-encoded at load from bf16 or fp8 to nvfp4 or fp8 (load(..., encode=)), and the facts record it (draft_encoding). Decode rows (up to 16) take the prompt rows' activations by default (decode_activations; bf16 for weight-only decode rows) and keep each row's bits alone and batched. Captured rounds (rounds:projections) and prompt chunks (prompts:projections): every decode and prompt path runs on buffers sized at load without host synchronization, and every call path of a matrix runs once at load (Triton compiles, cuBLAS's first use of a shape, CUDA modules), so no request compiles; a shape the warm-up did not meet raises inside a capture. AWQ and GPTQ INT4 matrices (load formats awq and gptq: qweight, qzeros, scales, GPTQ's g_idx act order and zero_offset) load into crit's INT4 rows with a zero point a group through decode-gemv's repack (format int4_zp in the facts), W4A16: decode rows on mma-rows' INT4 tile or decode-gemv's INT4 GEMV as gemv says (crossover from their sweep reports), prompt rows on mma-rows' prompt tile. With prompt_gemm native the quantized prompt GEMMs run on crit's GEMMs accumulated in the tensor cores (auto, the default: where they measured faster, MXFP8 W8A8) (fp8-block-rows' and int-block-experts' gemm-native; not row invariant: row_invariance prompt_rows false).

group.description: weights per FP32 scale, for int8 and int4

four_over_six.description: for nvfp4: scale blocks to 4 instead of 6 where that lowers the error

activations.description: on the device, what a stored NVFP4 matrix multiplies: NVFP4 activations (W4A4: prompt rows through cuBLASLt, decode rows as decode_activations says) or 16-bit ones (weight only: GEMVs for decode rows, the matrix decoded for the prompt GEMMs)

fp8_activations.description: FP8 matrices' prompt rows: fp8 (W8A8: each activation row in E4M3 by its own scale, cuBLASLt with the row and column scales in its epilogue), or bf16 (W8A16: the E4M3 weights widened exactly to BF16 times the 16-bit activations, FP32 sums, the row scale after; on the tile up to tile_rows, past it the matrix a chunk of rows at a time for a BF16 GEMM): an exact variant a preserve-mode engine may take where activation quantization costs too much quality. Decode rows with decode_activations prompt follow it. The facts give every format's arithmetic (prompt_arithmetic)

decode_activations.description: on the device, what decode rows (calls of up to the facts' row_invariance rows: decode steps, verify windows) of FP8 and W4A4 NVFP4 matrices multiply: prompt, the prompt rows' activations (each row quantized to E4M3, or to NVFP4 at the input scale), so a decoded token and the same token in a prompt (a replay, a prompt cache) differ only in their sums' order; bf16, the 16-bit activations themselves (weight only: W8A16, W4A16), closer to the unquantized model and further from the prompt rows. Weight-only NVFP4 (activations bf16) and MXFP8 matrices multiply 16-bit activations in both phases. With prompt, W4A4 NVFP4 decode rows run mma-rows' block-scaled FP4 MMA where the device has it (the sm_120 family; E2M1 codes with their block scales on both operands, FP32 sums, the prompt rows' arithmetic in another order), else the tile on the quantized values as BF16

decode_formats.description: comma-separated format=activations pairs (formats fp8 and nvfp4, activations prompt or bf16) that override decode_activations for the matrices of that format, chosen per matrix at load from its format, e.g. nvfp4=prompt,fp8=bf16: W4A4 NVFP4 decode rows on the prompt rows' NVFP4 activations (mma-rows' FP4 MMA where the device has it) and FP8 decode rows on 16-bit activations (W8A16: decode-gemv's dot GEMV with gemv auto); a format it does not name takes decode_activations. The facts' decode_activations (per format) and decode_kernels (per role) say which each matrix took

decode_rows.description: the most rows a decode call takes (8 to 16), each row's bits those of the row alone (the facts' row_invariance rows; 8 on the Triton GEMV): the CUDA-core GEMVs grow compute bound toward 16 rows on wide matrices (a vocabulary-wide FP8 head is about 2.6x cuBLASLt there), so a model that runs 9-16 decode rows mostly in such matrices may take 8 and send the rest as prompt rows

tile_rows.description: on mma-rows' tile (gemv mma), the most prompt rows a call sends through the tile too, 64 rows a kernel call: auto, by each matrix's prompt arithmetic as far as the tile beats its prompt path (weight-only prompts 64; W4A4, W8A8 and BF16 none: measured, device_matrices.AUTO_TILES), or one count for every matrix. A row gets the same bits in any call of up to that many rows where the decode and prompt arithmetic agree (the facts' row_invariance.rows: the fewest over the loaded matrices), so captured prompt buckets that size equal the unpadded chunk. Not for weight-only NVFP4 prompts in fp16_acc or fp8, nor with prompt_gemm fixed_tiles

prompt.description: with activations bf16, the prompt GEMMs' arithmetic: the matrix decoded to BF16 (FP32 accumulation), to FP16 accumulating in FP16 (twice the rate, FP16 out), or to FP8 rows against FP8 activation rows (rowwise scaled)

prompt_gemm.description: the GEMM prompt rows (calls of more rows than a decode call takes) go through: auto (the default), native for every prompt arithmetic (device_matrices.NATIVE_AUTO, every kind True: crit runs its own kernels, the libraries are yardsticks); native, every prompt arithmetic on crit's kernels: W8A8 FP8 matrices (each activation row in E4M3 by its own scale) on fp8-block-rows' gemm-native, MXFP8 matrices with mxfp8_activations mxfp8 on its block-scaled MXFP8 MMAs (sm_120a), W4A4 NVFP4 matrices on int-block-experts' gemm-native (block-scaled FP4 MMAs on the decode rows' NVFP4 activations at the input scale), BF16 matrices and the BF16-decoded chunks of weight-only ones (W8A16, W4A16 with prompt bf16, MXFP8 with 16-bit activations) on fixed-tile-gemm; the quantized GEMMs NOT the declared order and not row invariant (the tuning's configuration follows the prompt's length: the facts' row_invariance prompt_rows false, prompt_kernels naming each role's kernel); weight-only NVFP4 prompts in fp8 on fp8-block-rows' per-channel GEMM over FP8-decoded chunks; weight-only prompts in fp16_acc (FP16 sums, no crit kernel) and a matrix whose crit kernel is not here as provider; provider, torch's (cuBLAS(Lt) picks its algorithm, and so a row's sums, by the row count); fixed_tiles, for BF16 matrices and weight-only ones with prompt bf16, one whose tiles never change an output's order (crit's kernel fixed-tile-gemm; one row at a time through torch where it is not here, correct and much slower); pinned, for every format (W4A4, W8A8, W8A16, W4A16 with prompt bf16, MXFP8, BF16), crit's GEMMs in one configuration a matrix shape (native's quantized GEMMs built with their default knobs, one configuration for every token count, and launched as for device_matrices.PIN_ROWS tokens whatever the call's count, longer calls in pieces of that many; 16-bit operands on fixed-tile-gemm), so a prompt row's bits are the same at every prompt length (one prompt row a call through the provider where crit's GEMM for a matrix is not here, correct and much slower); pinned_cublaslt, the same row invariance through cuBLASLt with one split-K-free algorithm per GEMM shape and format, chosen at load and run for every row count (crit's kernel pinned-gemm, a library's GEMM: a yardstick for pinned); tile, for every format with gemv mma (W4A16 with prompt bf16), mma-rows' prompt tile: each prompt row multiplies the decode rows' activations in the decode tile's order, so every output has the bits the same row gets as a decode row (the facts' row_invariance prompt_exact: a scored token's log-probability is the served one's, preserve mode's exact honesty) at GEMM-like weight reuse; a matrix the decode tile does not take, or a kernel build without the prompt tile, goes through the provider and the facts say prompt_exact false. With fixed_tiles, pinned, pinned_cublaslt or tile a prompt row's result is the same at every prompt length, in any chunk, padded bucket or pass shared with other sequences (the facts' row_invariance prompt_rows), and prompt rows skip mma-rows' tile (tile_rows applies to decode rows only)

prompt_roles.description: with activations bf16, comma-separated role=arithmetic pairs (bf16, fp16_acc, fp8) that override `prompt` for the matrices a model loads with that role (load(tensors, format, role)), e.g. gate_up=fp8 for FP8 rows on the widest matrix and `prompt` elsewhere; a role it does not name takes `prompt`; prompt_gemm fixed_tiles applies to the bf16 ones

gemv.description: the decode rows' kernel: auto, each matrix's fastest measured one: FP8 matrices' 16-bit decode rows (W8A16) on decode-gemv's dot GEMV (a Triton program of 16 rows by a block of the matrix on tensor cores, a fixed split of K added in order; faster than the tile from 8 rows on, level below; K a multiple of 128), W4A4 decode rows on mma-rows' block-scaled FP4 MMA (the sm_120 family; K a multiple of 128), every other matrix as mma (the facts' decode_kernels name each role's); mma, mma-rows' tensor-core tile (every format, the weights read once a call whatever the rows, the prompt rows' quantized activations; K a multiple of 32), else as native; native, decode-gemv's CUDA-core GEMVs (its Triton GEMV for NVFP4 matrices whose width is no multiple of 32); triton, its Triton GEMV for NVFP4 (BF16 rows then run a row at a time through torch); where no kernel is here, the torch fallbacks (the matrix's exact values, one row at a time). Each keeps FP32 sums and a row's bits alone and batched; their orders differ, so a process uses one a matrix. crossover: each matrix's decode calls of up to its measured crossover on decode-gemv's CUDA-core GEMV, longer ones on mma-rows' tile (as mma): the crossover is the most rows at which the GEMV's tuned time is no more than the tile's at every row count both sweeps timed at the matrix's shape (their reports beside the engine's tuning, CRIT_KERNEL_TUNING, swept on this device's model), 0 without them or for decode rows on quantized activations (every call on the tile); a row then keeps its bits across calls of up to the crossover and across longer ones, not between the two (the facts' row_invariance rows is the crossover, decode_crossover names it per role), so it suits single-sequence decoding without verify windows; not with prompt_gemm tile.

mxfp8_activations.description: what MXFP8 matrices multiply: bf16, 16-bit activations (W8A16, the stored values exact in BF16); mxfp8, MXFP8's own activations as modelopt MXFP8 checkpoints declare them (W8A8: each 32 inputs of a row in E4M3 under a shared power of two 2^(floor(log2 amax) - 8), fp8-block-rows' quantizer): prompt rows on fp8-block-rows' block-scaled gemm-native with prompt_gemm native (else the quantized values as 16-bit rows through the W8A16 paths, the same arithmetic in another order), decode rows with decode_activations prompt on the quantized values (exact in BF16) through the W8A16 GEMV or the tile

kernels.name: decode-gemv
kernels.fallback: torch: the matrix decoded a chunk of rows at a time to its exact values, one activation row per GEMM (FP32 sums, the inverse global scale once); decoders as torch operations with the kernel's bits

kernels.name: fp8-block-rows
kernels.fallback: with prompt_gemm native: FP8 prompt rows through the provider's GEMM (cuBLASLt, the same W8A8 arithmetic in its order), with pinned one row a call; MXFP8 activations quantized in torch (the kernel's bits) and multiplied as 16-bit rows

kernels.name: fixed-tile-gemm
kernels.fallback: torch: one prompt row per GEMM, so a row keeps its bits whatever rows share the call (correct, much slower)

kernels.name: int-block-experts
kernels.fallback: with prompt_gemm native: W4A4 prompt rows through cuBLASLt's block-scaled NVFP4 GEMM (the same arithmetic in its order), with pinned one row a call

kernels.name: mma-rows
kernels.fallback: the CUDA-core GEMVs of crit's kernel decode-gemv for decode rows (or their torch fallbacks), the prompt path for every prompt row

kernels.name: pinned-gemm
kernels.fallback: with prompt_gemm pinned_cublaslt: one prompt row a call through the provider's GEMM (one algorithm for every row, so a row keeps its bits; correct, much slower)
